public_rationale: Marcus gave no deadline for budgets to tighten. Futurum released its 2H 2026 CIO survey of 1,636 enterprise technology decision makers on 2026-09-10, after the 2026-05-28 post. In that survey, 46.9% of organizations reported AI spend above their planned budget, and 5.6% reported spend below plan (e1). Of the 767 organizations over plan, 47.6% asked for more budget, 43.3% absorbed the overrun to settle later, and 17.2% paused or reduced the AI initiative (e2). These figures do not show a clear net share of enterprises cutting or capping AI budgets. They also do not show an absolute fall in AI spending. So the early-resolution rule is not met. Because there is no deadline, the forecast cannot be contradicted yet.
limitations: "Tighten" is vague. It could mean caps, cuts, slower growth, or more scrutiny.
The evidence is one survey press release. The full Futurum report and other surveys (Gartner, McKinsey, BCG) were not read.
The three response shares for over-plan organizations add up to more than 100%, so the categories overlap. The press release does not say how many organizations chose each response alone.
The survey measures spend against plan. It does not show whether planned budgets were cut or capped.

conditions: especially once people realize how costly agents are

statement.excerpt: Budgets will tighten, especially when people realize just how costly agents (which burn orders of magnitudes more tokens) are.
statement.document_title: Breaking: bad news for three of the biggest IPOs in history

from_speaker: "especially when people realize just how costly agents ... are"
our_interpretation: "Budgets" means enterprise budgets for generative AI tokens and tools, in context of tokenmaxxing at companies.
"Tighten" means companies broadly cap, cut, or slow AI spending relative to plans, not just a few firms adding per-seat limits.
The "especially when" clause is an amplifier, not a precondition, so the forecast is treated as unconditional.
criteria.support_condition: Broad evidence after 2026-05-28 (major surveys, spending data, or widespread reported policies) that enterprises are cutting, capping, or slowing AI token and tool budgets.
criteria.contradiction_condition: With no deadline, the forecast can't be finally contradicted. Sustained evidence that enterprise AI budgets kept expanding would weigh against it but would not settle it.

evidence.excerpt: About 46.9% of organizations report actual AI spend exceeding their planned AI budget, according to new research from The Futurum Group, compared with just 5.6% that came in below plan.
evidence.explanation: By the second half of 2026, AI spend was running over plan at nearly half of enterprises. That points away from broad tightening so far, but it does not settle an open-ended forecast.

evidence.excerpt: Among the 767 organizations running over plan, 47.6% ask for more budget and 43.3% absorb the overrun and settle it later, while only 17.2% pause or reduce the AI initiative itself.
evidence.explanation: A minority of over-budget firms are cutting back, which partly fits Marcus's view. Most are funding the overrun instead.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: A major survey or spending dataset published after 2026-05-28 that shows a clear net share of enterprises cutting or capping AI token and tool budgets, or an absolute fall in enterprise AI spending.
